exercises.title: 1. Squat · 6–8 reps
exercises.instructions:
Start with a bodyweight squat: feet about shoulder-width, sit your hips back and down, keep heels planted, then stand. Knees follow the direction of your toes. Stop at a comfortable depth.

With a bell: hold it close to your chest with both hands for a goblet squat. Easier: sit down and stand up from a sturdy chair or fixed bench, if available. Do not use a rolling chair.

exercises.title: 2. Kettlebell deadlift · 8–10 reps
exercises.instructions:
Place the bell between your feet. Soften your knees and push your hips back to reach the handle with both hands. Keep your back in its natural position and arms long. Push through your feet to stand tall; lower slowly by moving the hips back again. Do not lean backward at the top.

Easier: practice the hinge without a bell, reaching your hips toward a wall behind you. If reaching the floor makes your back round, use this version until the movement is comfortable.

exercises.title: 3. Wall push-up · 6–10 reps
exercises.instructions:
Put hands on a wall at chest height, slightly wider than shoulders. Walk feet back, keep your body in a straight line, bend elbows to bring your chest toward the wall, then press away. Keep elbows angled back rather than flared straight out.

Easier: move feet closer to the wall. Harder: move them farther back, or use a sturdy fixed bench for incline push-ups.

exercises.title: 4. One-arm kettlebell row · 8 reps each side
exercises.instructions:
Use a staggered stance with the bell beside your front foot. Hinge forward and support your free forearm on your front thigh. Keep your back steady; pull the bell toward your hip, then lower slowly. Keep shoulders level and avoid twisting.

Use the lightest bell. If it is too heavy to move smoothly, leave this exercise out until you have a suitable weight.

exercises.title: 5. Calf raise · 10–12 reps
exercises.instructions: Stand on flat ground beside a wall for balance. Rise onto the balls of both feet, pause briefly, then lower slowly. Keep your ankles upright and the movement comfortable. Start without a bell.

exercises.title: 6. Suitcase carry · 20–30 seconds each side
exercises.instructions:
Hold one bell at your side like a suitcase. Stand tall, keep shoulders level, and walk slowly down a clear section of court. Turn carefully, set the bell down with a hip hinge, then change hands. Do not lean away from the weight.

Easier: hold it while standing still for 10–20 seconds, or use a lighter bell.

exercises.title: 1. Glute bridge · 8–10 reps
exercises.instructions: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat about hip-width apart. Gently tighten your stomach and squeeze your glutes to lift your hips until shoulders, hips, and knees form a line. Lower slowly. Avoid arching your lower back; keep this bodyweight-only.

exercises.title: 2. Supported split squat · 5–6 reps each side
exercises.instructions:
Hold a wall for balance. Take a short staggered stance, both feet on the floor. Bend both knees to lower a few inches, then push up. Keep your front heel down and hips facing forward. Use a small comfortable range.

Easier: substitute 6 bodyweight squats from workout A. Keep split squats unweighted to start; if they leave you sore for Saturday, use squats or skip them that week.

exercises.title: 3. Wall push-up · 6–8 reps
exercises.instructions: Use the same technique as Monday, with an easy foot position. Stop well before your arms tire out.

exercises.title: 4. Calf raise · 8–10 reps
exercises.instructions: Use both feet on flat ground, with a wall for balance. Rise and lower slowly. Keep this lighter than Monday.

exercises.title: 5. Bird dog · 5 reps each side
exercises.instructions:
On hands and knees, gently brace your stomach. Slowly reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back, keeping hips level and back still. Hold 2–3 seconds, then return and switch sides.

Easier: move just one arm or one leg at a time. Use a folded towel or mat under your knees if needed.

progression:
Weeks 1–2: one easy set per exercise. Weeks 3–4: add a second set to Monday's exercises if soreness settles within 24–48 hours and runs feel normal. Friday stays at one set initially. From week 5: maintain two sets Monday and one or two easy sets Friday, depending on recovery.

Reach the top of the rep range comfortably for two sessions before increasing weight. Increase only one thing at a time: reps, sets, or weight. With a heavier bell, return to the low end of the rep range. If the next bell is too heavy, keep your current bell; you do not need to keep adding load.

Protect the long run: if Friday makes Saturday harder, move workout B to Wednesday, halve its sets, or skip its leg exercises that week. On cutback weeks, halve Monday's sets too. During the final two weeks, keep strength easy; in race week, follow the short mobility and activation sessions on the weekly checklist instead of workouts A and B.

Use the court for easy walking and carries. Basketball games, sprints, jumps, and hard cutting drills add leg fatigue; they are extra training, not recovery. Keep them out of these strength sessions. Swings, cleans, and snatches are unnecessary for this plan.

Muscle effort and mild next-day soreness can happen. Stop an exercise for sharp or joint pain, dizziness, or loss of control. If soreness changes how you run or lasts more than 48 hours, reduce the next session.

guide.title: Your normal week
guide.body:
Monday: 20–30 minutes strength. Tuesday: easy run/walk. Wednesday: rest or relaxed walking. Thursday: run/walk. Friday: 15–25 minutes light strength. Saturday: easy long run/walk. Sunday: rest.

Open the Strength workouts tab for Monday's workout A and Friday's lighter workout B, using your kettlebells, a wall, and court space. Start with one easy set. Move Friday strength to Wednesday if needed.

guide.title: Time commitment by phase
guide.body: Weeks 1–4: about 2–3 hours/week. Weeks 5–8: 2.5–3.5 hours. Weeks 9–14: 3–4.5 hours. Weeks 15–23: 3.5–5 hours; the 12 mile peak may take 2.5–3 hours by itself. Weeks 24–26: taper, about 2–3.5 hours including race week. Add travel, changing and showering separately.

guide.title: When to adjust
guide.body:
Repeat a week when recovery is poor, effort rises, or the next step feels too large. Reduce a long run by 20–30% or replace it with walking when needed. If you miss a week, return to the last comfortable week; after a longer gap, step back further. Never stack missed sessions.

Stop if pain changes your gait or worsens while running. Persistent pain needs assessment before progression. Chest pain, fainting or unusual severe breathlessness require prompt medical care. Heat, ice, illness and poor sleep are reasons to slow down or shorten the session.

guide.title: Goal pace without forcing it
guide.body:
2:10 for 13.1 miles means about 9:55 per mile including every walk break and stop. Running segments must be faster than this average. Do not use goal pace for easy runs.

From week 15, if recovering well, try 3 × 5 minutes of controlled, goal-average run/walk effort within Thursday's session, with 3 easy minutes between. Keep the rest easy; skip this during cutback weeks. Extend to 2 × 10 minutes only when comfortable. Finish healthy is the primary goal; keep 2:10 only if training supports it.

guide.title: Long runs, fueling and race day
guide.body:
For runs longer than 75–90 minutes, practice small, regular carbohydrate portions and drinking to thirst. Use products and amounts your stomach tolerates; test them before race day. Practice your shoes, socks and walk ratio.

Use your practiced ratio from the start of the race. Keep the first 3 miles restrained, settle through mile 10, then decide whether you have more. Choose a comfortable finish over chasing the clock when conditions or readiness disagree. Reduce strength loads in the taper and skip heavy strength in race week.

guide.title: Plan notes and sources
guide.body:
This is a reconstructed, Galloway-inspired comeback plan, not an official Jeff Galloway schedule or a verbatim recovery of the earlier chat. Starting context: 43, returning after a long break, recent hard 2.5 mile run. Dates run from October 26, 2026 through race week April 19–25, 2027.

Jeff Galloway: Run Walk Run · Half marathon training
